title: National ML/TF risk assessment working group meets
detail: The Financial Information Unit convened the working group preparing Mongolia's National Risk Assessment on money laundering and terrorist financing to harmonise sectoral vulnerability scoring across sub-groups.

title: Woman dies in ger fire in Bayanzurkh district
detail: A 58-year-old woman was killed when a fire broke out in a ger in Bayanzurkh district of Ulaanbaatar on Wednesday afternoon; the cause was under investigation, NEMA said.
attribution: National Emergency Management Agency via Xinhua

title: Extreme winter weather (dzud) hits 9+ provinces
detail: Severe cold and snow cover affected at least nine of Mongolia's 21 provinces, including Tuv, threatening livestock grazing, according to NEMA as reported by Xinhua.

title: AML/CFT council adopts 2026 FATF-style follow-up report
detail: More than 30 representatives from 13 authorities at the AML/CFT Cooperation Council adopted Mongolia's draft 2026 Follow-Up Report, according to the FIU.

title: Criminal cases up 6.3% in 2025 to 47,480
detail: The National Statistics Office reported 47,480 criminal cases in 2025, up 6.3%, with 43,800 victims; traffic-safety crimes rose 43.2%.

title: 78 foreigners from 12 countries deported in January
detail: The Immigration Agency said 78 foreign nationals (53 Chinese, 11 Russian and others) were deported for visa or residence overstays, unauthorised work and other violations, with 3-5 year re-entry bans; it reported 1,222 deportations in the previous year.

title: Drug crimes up 21.6% in 2025, 417 arrested
detail: The General Prosecutor's Office said 551 drug-related crimes were registered in 2025, up 21.6% on 2024, and 417 people were apprehended, over 40% aged 25-35.
attribution: State General Prosecutor's Office via Xinhua

title: Ulaanbaatar AQI 204, world's most polluted major city
detail: IQAir ranked Ulaanbaatar the most polluted major city globally with a US AQI of 204 (very unhealthy), driven largely by coal heating and winter inversions; improvement to moderate was forecast.

title: Dzud kills 26,300+ livestock in January
detail: The National Statistics Office said more than 26,300 head of livestock died in January, with heavy losses in Uvs, Bayan-Ulgii, Zavkhan and Uvurkhangai; at least 11 of 21 provinces were under dzud conditions.

title: All road crossings with China closed for Tsagaan Sar
detail: Customs said all 10 road crossings with China, including Zamiin-Uud and Gashuunsukhait, would close 17-20 February and some Russian crossings 18-20 February, while Zamyn-Uud rail traffic and Altanbulag continued operating.

title: Van falls through ice on Khuvsgul Lake, two dead
detail: A UAZ-452 van carrying seven people plunged through an ice crack in the Khachim area of Dalai Zakh on Khuvsgul Lake; one adult and one child died and five were rescued, and officials warned against driving on frozen lakes.

title: Winter storm: 31 m/s winds, -48C, 5 dead
detail: A severe winter storm on 21-24 Feb brought heavy snow, winds up to 31 m/s and temperatures as low as -48C; 5 deaths and 56 injuries were recorded, per the IFRC DREF operation MDRMN021 cited by Wikipedia.
attribution: IFRC DREF report as summarised by Wikipedia

title: Khovd resident charged over transporting endangered Altai snowcock
detail: Environmental police charged a Khovd resident under the wildlife-trafficking article of the Criminal Code for unlawfully transporting Altai snowcock in January; the case went to prosecutors and the suspect paid 434,000 MNT in compensation.
attribution: Police / Environmental Police Department, as reported by The UB Post

title: Severe sludge pollution of Tuul River below UB treatment plant
detail: Sludge deposits 20-50 cm thick were found along about 21 km of the Tuul River downstream of Ulaanbaatar's Central Wastewater Treatment Plant (built 1964, not modernised), per city officials; a new plant was due in May 2026.
attribution: Deputy Governor of Ulaanbaatar via Montsame

title: 14 forest and steppe fires burn 21,175 ha so far in 2026
detail: NEMA said 14 forest and steppe fires had been recorded since the start of the year, mainly in eastern Dornod, Sukhbaatar and Khentii provinces, affecting 21,175 hectares, with human negligence the main cause.
attribution: National Emergency Management Agency via Xinhua

title: Court confiscates official's unexplained 45m MNT vehicle
detail: The IAAC said a first-instance court ordered MNT 45,000,000, the value of a Lexus RX-450 held by an unnamed public official who could not explain its lawful source, transferred to the state budget under an unexplained-wealth mechanism of the Anti-Corruption Law.

title: Wildfire warning as over half of provinces extremely dry
detail: The national meteorological agency warned of heightened wildfire risk with more than half of the 21 provinces in extremely dry conditions; three wildfires were being fought in Dornod and Khentii.
agency: National Agency for Meteorology and Environmental Monitoring
attribution: National Agency for Meteorology and Environmental Monitoring via Xinhua

title: Telecom firm cites 694bn MNT online-fraud losses in 2025
detail: In a press release launching an anti-fraud awareness campaign, Unitel Group said online fraud cost Mongolians 694 billion MNT in 2025, that fraud cases rose 296% over five years and that digital crimes exceeded 30% of recorded crimes; the release does not cite an official source for these figures.
attribution: Figures claimed by Unitel Group (private telecom operator), unsourced

title: 48 forest and steppe fires, 229,006 ha burned by mid-April
detail: As of 12 April, 48 fires had hit 32 soums in eight provinces and two capital districts, affecting about 229,006 ha (704 ha forest); 8 people from 3 households and some 2,000 livestock were moved, and over 1,650 personnel with 264 vehicles were deployed, per the report.
attribution: National Emergency Management Agency figures, as reported by The UB Post

title: 48 e-scooter and moped accidents in four days after road authorisation
detail: The National Traumatology and Orthopedics Research Center recorded 48 accidents involving scooters, mopeds and similar vehicles on 10-14 April after they were authorised on roads, with 87.5% of injured not wearing helmets; it logged 2,792 such injuries in 2025.
agency: National Traumatology and Orthopedics Research Center
attribution: National Traumatology and Orthopedics Research Center

title: Grassfires in Zavkhan and Khentii extinguished
detail: A grassfire in Otgon soum, Zavkhan, started on 21 April and was out by the next morning, and another in Delgerkhaan soum, Khentii, on 22 April was contained within 37 minutes; NEMA warned dry conditions persist.
attribution: National Emergency Management Agency, as reported by The UB Post

title: Low rainfall, heat forecast for eastern region May-July
detail: The Institute of Plant and Agricultural Sciences forecast low precipitation and above-average temperatures in June-July in the eastern region, 50-70 mm+ rain in the central zone and above-average June rain in the west.
agency: Institute of Plant and Agricultural Sciences

title: Cabinet suspends Tuul Expressway project
detail: The government halted the Tuul Highway project after 300+ petitions, pending a law-enforcement and oversight review of officials linked to it, according to the Cabinet Secretariat.

title: IAAC says USD 13.9m in stolen assets recovered since 2017
detail: IAAC chief commissioner Z.Baasannyam said the agency has recovered USD 13.9 million in stolen assets through international cooperation since 2017, citing a case of GBP 1.18 million in bribes laundered via Latvian and BVI accounts into a London flat, and MNT 11.3 billion (USD 5.7 million) recovered from the Isle of Man.
attribution: Claim by IAAC chief commissioner (interview with Udriin Sonin)

title: Customs inspector held in bribery and money-laundering probe
detail: The IAAC arrested a state customs inspector accused of taking a 50 million MNT bribe from the director of a freight-forwarding company, who was also detained; the case is opened under money laundering, abuse of power and bribe-taking articles of the Criminal Code, per the report.
attribution: Independent Authority Against Corruption, as reported by The UB Post

title: M5.5 quake and aftershocks strike Zereg soum, Khovd
detail: A magnitude 5.5 earthquake (GFZ reported 5.9) struck about 26 km southeast of Zereg soum centre, followed by M4.2 and M3.9 tremors; it was felt in 15 soums with no damage or casualties reported, per the Institute of Astronomy and Geophysics.
attribution: Institute of Astronomy and Geophysics, Mongolian Academy of Sciences; GFZ epicentre

title: 2,340 foreigners involved in visa violations in four months
detail: Authorities processed 994 immigration violations involving 2,340 foreign nationals from 34 countries in January-April, 64% of them Chinese, mostly residence-permit and overstay cases.
agency: Department of Foreign Citizens and Nationality
attribution: Department of Foreign Citizens and Nationality

title: Girl, 3, dies after falling into abandoned mining borehole
detail: A three-year-old girl fell into an abandoned 30 m deep, 30 cm wide mining borehole in Zaamar soum; more than 100 rescuers worked 58 hours and recovered her body on 30 May, NEMA said. The incident prompted a nationwide hazard inspection.
attribution: National Emergency Management Agency via Xinhua

title: FMD confirmed in Bulgan soum, Khovd
detail: The Khovd governor's office confirmed foot-and-mouth disease in 35 cattle of seven herder households; about 5,500 livestock in the zone were at risk and quarantine was imposed.

title: IAAC, US officials discuss crypto tracing and asset recovery
detail: IAAC leadership met the US Embassy legal attache and an IRS Criminal Investigation official to discuss asset recovery in money-laundering and corruption cases, cryptocurrency investigation and asset-freezing techniques, and cybercrime cooperation.

title: Fraud now about half of reported crimes in Ulaanbaatar
detail: The head of the Capital City Police Department told a meeting with the city council chairman that fraud (online shopping scams, phishing for bank details, fake lottery and giveaway schemes) has risen sharply and now makes up about half of reported crimes in the city; no case counts or loss figures were given.
attribution: Claim by Capital City Police Department head

title: FMD outbreak in Dundgovi (Gurvansaikhan, Adaatsag)
detail: Dundgovi's governor's office reported FMD in Gurvansaikhan and Adaatsag soums, with quarantine, disinfection and vaccination under way; outbreaks also reported in Khovd and Bayan-Ulgii.

title: SAT-1 FMD strain detected for first time; Khovd on alert
detail: The Ministry of Food, Agriculture and Light Industry said the highly virulent SAT-1 strain was identified in Mongolia for the first time; Khovd imposed indefinite heightened preparedness and banned large gatherings.
agency: Ministry of Food, Agriculture and Light Industry

title: 1,230+ animals culled over FMD in west
detail: More than 1,230 livestock were culled in Bayan-Ulgii and Khovd over SAT-1 FMD, and serotype O was reported in six of 21 provinces, according to the General Authority for Veterinary Services.

title: Smuggled Tarbosaurus skeleton returned from France
detail: A Tarbosaurus bataar skeleton and other fossils in 15 crates, illegally excavated in Umnugovi and smuggled out around 2006 with forged documents per police, were handed back after 13 years in French custody.
agency: Prosecutor General's Office; General Police Department; General Customs Administration

title: OSCE flags Mongolian victims of trafficking into cyber-scam operations
detail: During a follow-up visit to Mongolia, the OSCE Special Representative on trafficking held a workshop on trafficking for forced criminality in cyber-scam operations, citing OSCE research with documented cases involving Mongolian victims; no victim numbers were published.
attribution: OSCE Special Representative for Combating Trafficking in Human Beings

title: Child-safety campaign finds nearly 15,000 hazards
detail: Following the Zaamar borehole death, inspections of 7,844 sites between 30 May and 15 June found 14,977 safety violations, of which 11,999 were fixed, according to the Authority of Child and Family Development Protection.
agency: Authority of Child and Family Development Protection
attribution: Authority of Child and Family Development Protection, as reported by The UB Post

title: Protesters briefly block Oyu Tolgoi copper exports
detail: Members of a group called the Radical Reform Movement blocked the highway used by trucks carrying copper concentrate from Oyu Tolgoi to the Chinese border, demanding a larger revenue share; exports resumed after a brief disruption. No arrests or injuries were reported.
place: Oyu Tolgoi mine road, Khanbogd soum

title: Khaan Quest 2026 multinational exercise opens
detail: The 23rd Khaan Quest peacekeeping exercise opened at the Five Hills Training Area near Ulaanbaatar with more than 1,100 personnel from 18 countries, running to 3 July.

title: Orkhon, Khuder, Yuruu rivers above warning levels
detail: NEMA said water levels on the Orkhon, Khuder and Yuruu rivers rose 50-100 cm in a day, exceeding warning thresholds, and warned of further rises after cold rain and wet snow.

title: Unseasonal cold rain, wet snow; ground temps below -5C
detail: Cold rain and wet snowfall across Mongolia in late June pushed ground-level temperatures below -5C, according to NEMA as reported in coverage of its flood warning.

title: Cabinet backs new defence cooperation pact with South Korea
detail: The Cabinet supported a draft defence cooperation agreement with the Republic of Korea updating the 1999 accord, covering military visits, training and regular joint exercises.

title: Heat above +35C in west and Gobi; +40C in Gobi-Altai, Bayankhongor
detail: Forecasts reported by Montsame said temperatures would pass +35C in western and Gobi aimags and exceed +40C in southern Gobi-Altai and Bayankhongor, with UB at +28 to +30C.
attribution: Weather forecast as reported by Montsame

title: Under-18s banned from riding e-scooters, mopeds, e-bikes
detail: Amended traffic safety rules effective 1 July bar minors from light electric vehicles, with parents and rental operators liable; the trauma centre recorded 754 injuries in January-May, per the Ministry of Road and Transport.
attribution: Ministry of Road and Transport via Xinhua

title: Khalkh River exceeds danger level, severe flooding
detail: NAMEM and NEMA said the Khalkh River at Yalalt surpassed the danger level by 15 cm, causing severe flooding.
place: Khalkh River at Yalalt, Sumber soum

title: Multiple rivers 5-30 cm over flood levels
detail: Kharaa, Onon, Kherlen (incl. Baganuur), Khovd, Kharkhiraa and Tuul (Lun soum) rivers exceeded flood thresholds by 5-30 cm; further rises forecast for Tuul, Onon and Kherlen, per NAMEM and NEMA.
place: Kharaa, Onon, Kherlen, Khovd, Kharkhiraa, Tuul rivers

title: Israeli tourists attacked by axe-wielding man at campsite
detail: An intoxicated man shouting antisemitic slogans attacked a group of six Israeli tourists with an axe at a campsite in northern Mongolia; one man suffered a fractured jaw. Mongolian officials condemned the attack; the group declined to file a police complaint, per Hebrew media reports.
attribution: Hebrew media reports via The Times of Israel

title: Drowning and river rescues in north prompt water-safety warning
detail: NEMA reported four young men rescued by motorboat from the Selenge River in Bulgan province on 23 July, and a 22-year-old man drowned in the Kharaa River in Selenge province after a multi-day search; it urged people to use designated swimming areas.
attribution: National Emergency Management Agency, as reported by The UB Post

title: Selenge, Chuluut, Baidrag rising; Tuul, Kharkhiraa above flood level
detail: Rivers rose 10-55 cm in a day with 10-20 cm more forecast on Selenge, Chuluut and Baidrag; Kharkhiraa and Tuul remained 5-10 cm above flood level, and the public was told to avoid riverbanks.
place: Selenge, Chuluut, Baidrag, Kharkhiraa, Tuul rivers
attribution: Flood warning as reported by Montsame

title: Mongolia-Russia joint border inspection 85% complete
detail: President Khurelsukh inspected work in Khuvsgul; the joint commission is replacing 1,620 markers on the 3,543 km border and 85% of engineering work is done, including renewed Marker No. 350.
agency: Joint Border Inspection Commission; Office of the President

title: State Emergency Commission reviews winter/dzud preparedness
detail: The State Emergency Commission, chaired by the Deputy PM, reviewed winter preparedness and backed amending the Disaster Protection Law to give local governments more financial authority in emergencies.

title: Flooding in Ulaanbaatar area: 1 dead, 189 displaced
detail: GDACS recorded authorities' reports of flooding in the Ulaanbaatar area on 1-3 Aug with one death and 189 people displaced (green alert).

title: Petrol purchases capped at 50,000 MNT under odd-even plate rule
detail: The energy minister limited AI-92 petrol sales to 50,000 MNT per vehicle with odd-even plate purchase days from 4 August, citing disrupted Russian supply after Russia suspended gasoline exports until 1 January 2027.
agency: Ministry of Energy and Mineral Resources
attribution: Minister of Energy and Mineral Resources, as reported by The UB Post

title: Fuel supply disruption hits flights and road transport
detail: Tourism associations warned that a fuel supply shortage was disrupting domestic and international flights, road transport and tours at peak season, and sought an urgent inter-ministry meeting.

title: Mongolian herder held in Russia on espionage suspicion
detail: A Mongolian herder detained by Russian authorities while crossing the border in mid-February 2026 has been held for seven months on suspicion of espionage, AKIpress reported citing Udriin Sonin.

title: Illegal marmot hunting persists despite inspections
detail: Environment officials and the Ecological Police Division said marmot poaching shows little sign of declining despite relocation of 500-700 marmots a year; inspections are under way at habitats and checkpoints. No case figures were given.
attribution: Ministry of Environment and Climate Change; Ecological Police Division

title: 13 internationally wanted fugitives returned to Mongolia
detail: The National Police Agency said 13 citizens on the international wanted list were repatriated to Mongolia in July; details of their alleged offences were not published in the open excerpt.

title: UNEP, Mongolia launch USD 2m animal-disease project
detail: UNEP announced a USD 2 million joint project with the government to study the spread of infectious animal diseases and reduce outbreaks.
agency: UNEP; Ministry of Environment and Climate Change

title: Early September frost and wet snow forecast in mountains
detail: Meteorologists warned of sharp night-time drops, frost and early wet snow in mountainous regions in September, and herders were advised to prepare fodder; spring sowing had been delayed by wet snow.

title: Mongolia joins GlobE Network model agreement on corruption cases
detail: At a meeting in Vienna (25-28 August) the IAAC joined a model agreement among GlobE Network law-enforcement members for rapid, secure exchange of information and mutual assistance on transnational corruption cases.
attribution: Independent Authority Against Corruption, as reported by The UB Post

title: Early influenza vaccination campaign, 500,000 doses
detail: The Health Ministry began free flu vaccination on 3 Sept with 500,000 doses at 600+ facilities for young children, pregnant women, over-65s and chronically ill, noting flu peaks in Jan-Feb.

title: Nationwide automatic air-quality monitoring network completed
detail: Automatic stations now cover Ulaanbaatar and all 21 aimag centres (PM2.5, PM10, SO2, NOx, O3, CO) under a USD 8.9 million Korea-backed project; data are public on agaar.gov.mn.
agency: Ministry of Environment and Climate Change

title: Mongolian, Chinese defence ministers agree to widen cooperation
detail: Defence Minister Damba Batlut met Chinese Defence Minister Dong Jun at the Beijing Xiangshan Forum and discussed expanding defence cooperation into new areas.

title: Officials warn fuel disruption could last two to three years
detail: A state secretary said Russian fuel supply disruptions could last 2-3 years due to refinery damage; the AI-92 shortage had run about 50 days, Ulaanbaatar stocks were critically low and four provinces faced delivery delays, while imports from South Korea and China were arranged.
agency: Ministry of Energy and Mineral Resources
attribution: State Secretary B.Dashpurev, as reported by The UB Post
